correspondence.correspondence: unresolved: model orientation only, no original cartographic component reading

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward elbow and long westward lower course
correspondence.finding: The model turns toward the northwest and then follows a long westward course. Bernard River is a regional discovery lead, but no acquired original map ties that name to this selected course or demonstrates all material junctions.
correspondence.correspondence: unresolved: model orientation only, no original cartographic component reading
correspondence.limits: No exact headwater, lake/stream link, branch junction, naming extent or terminal identity is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The retained model ends toward the west-northwest and its terminal class is sea. Regional prose identifies the Beaufort Sea as the destination of western Banks Island rivers, but the actual selected mouth branch, estuary/coastal waterbody, shore connection and final reach remain unverified.
correspondence.correspondence: unresolved: model orientation only, no original cartographic component reading
correspondence.limits: No exact headwater, lake/stream link, branch junction, naming extent or terminal identity is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Serrano setting
correspondence.finding: The selected head lies west of Serrano and east of the narrow Laguna La Amarga. It crosses the Serrano–San Joaquín road/rail corridor, bends south and then east across the Route 4 setting, and proceeds southeast through the Los Ceibos country. The maps do not show a named stream or a connection from Laguna La Amarga to this selected head.
correspondence.correspondence: Original bounded maps read. Landscape orientation supported; actual headward watercourse connection unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Coronel Charlone and Gronda
correspondence.finding: The line reaches the Coronel Charlone/Fernando Martí setting, crosses the Hipólito Bouchard–Santa Regina transport corridor, then passes west of Gronda and Emilio V. Bunge. It follows country east of the north–south meridian boundary after crossing into Buenos Aires. No river hydronym or connected course for this selected passage is established.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartography and bounded municipal place-name context read; hydrological connector pending.

correspondence.component_scope: San Bernardo to General Villegas
correspondence.finding: South of Gronda the modeled line passes the San Bernardo, Santa Elena and San José settings, turns markedly east, then southeast toward General Villegas. It crosses the road/rail network on the west and southwest side of the city, away from the Banderaló–Villa Sauze corridor farther west. Scattered lakes and marshes are mapped, without a continuous source-supported connection along this route.
correspondence.correspondence: Original geographic and historical inundation-map coverage; actual middle connection unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Tres Algarrobos–Pradere–Colonia Seré
correspondence.finding: The route continues through La Unión/San Eduardo and San Justo/La Fe marsh country west of Tres Algarrobos. It passes the Pradere lake and railway setting, then bends southeast and east through the La María Elisa/La Emilia/La Adelita country before crossing Route 70 and the railway east of Colonia Seré. Mapped lowlands and water bodies support local corridor setting, but not all intervening basin connections.
correspondence.correspondence: Original maps read; local wetland correspondence supported with material inter-basin gaps.

correspondence.component_scope: Francisco de Vitoria and lower lakes
correspondence.finding: East of Colonia Seré, the selected southward leg passes the La Negrita, Santa Susana, La Paz and Santa Lucía settings to Francisco de Vitoria. It approaches the elongated lake at Los Plátanos, bends east across the Mitre/El Guarany country and turns south by the San Félix–Santa Clotilde lakes, before heading east/southeast through Los Aromos. These are several mapped lakes and depressions, not a single established river name. Their complete interconnections remain unresolved.
correspondence.correspondence: Original lower cartography read; lake/depression geography supported, full connector evidence incomplete.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The final southeastward leg turns northeast inside an elongated unnamed lake north/northeast of Berutti, north of the railway and national Route 5 setting, west of the La Eva area. Both the 1:250,000 map and the 1:500,000 overview show the terminal lake setting. The selected line does not continue across the railway into the Hinojo–Las Tunas lakes to the south.
correspondence.correspondence: Original terminal cartography read. Terminal lake name remains unknown; no outlet continuation inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Branches, reservoirs and regional drainage
correspondence.finding: Only one selected mainstem FID is retained; no separate branch or reservoir passage is established. Provincial hydrology describes an interdunal, poorly drained plain with southward excess-water movement and engineered links. ADA prose separately describes the Quinto–La Dulce–Vidania–Cuero de Zorro chain toward Hinojo–Las Tunas. Those regional relationships do not establish the selected Serrano–Charlone route or its final lake connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Cartography plus bounded primary prose. No substitution of basin association for source correspondence.

remaining_material_gaps.gap: The original maps locate the selected head east of Laguna La Amarga and west of Serrano, then the route turns through Los Ceibos toward the Coronel Charlone/Fernando Martí settlement and transport crossing. A watercourse joining those settings along this selected headward route is not drawn or otherwise established. The separate La Amarga/Quinto association cannot supply that connector.

The modeled route passes the Gronda and San Bernardo settings, bends east across the Santa Elena–San José country and reaches the western/southwestern side of General Villegas. Original topography and independent event-inundation mapping show plains and separate depressions but do not establish this long selected hydrological connection.

remaining_material_gaps.component: General Villegas–Colonia Seré and lower inter-lake links
remaining_material_gaps.gap: The maps locate local marshes and elongate lakes along the San Justo/La Fe–Pradere–Colonia Seré–Francisco de Vitoria–Berutti corridor. Some selected stretches correspond to those wetland/lake settings, but the inter-basin transfers, including long eastward turns, are not established by the acquired sources. This is a component/connector evidence gap, not a demand for exact banks or every model vertex to fit.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastern initial feeder and southward turn into the upper receiving channel
correspondence.finding: The selected geometry begins on the plateau east of the mapped upper lake-and-channel corridor, initially runs west, then turns south. Both provincial original maps show the receiving channel and adjacent headwater drainage, but do not portray the complete selected initial feeder. Its connection is therefore not established by basin association, the report’s broad Aktaklin headwaters statement or model connectivity.
correspondence.correspondence: Material source/connector coverage pending, confined to this initial component.
correspondence.name_limit: No primary-map name is established for this selected initial feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper receiving channel and Nimpo Lake passage
correspondence.finding: Below the unresolved feeder, original provincial cartography shows the westward receiving drainage bending northwest by the Towdystan setting, entering the elongated Nimpo lake waters and leaving along the continuing northwestern corridor. Other nearby lake chains remain separate.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale below the initial gap.
correspondence.name_limit: Nimpo Lake is retained as a lake name. Small intervening channel and broadened-water names remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Anahim Lake, Abuntlet Lake and north-trending Dean corridor
correspondence.finding: Provincial maps show the selected continuation through the Anahim Lake setting and the connected Abuntlet lake/corridor north of the highway, then north past the lateral lake-and-tributary network toward the Tanswanket area. Inlets, lake passages, outlets and the continuation are visible at generalized scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Material lake and connecting-channel geography supported.
correspondence.name_limit: Separate lake names are preserved. The Dean label supports the receiving river corridor without renaming lakes or all minor channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwest turn, Tweedsmuir middle corridor and Itasyuko/Sigutlat branch
correspondence.finding: The structure map follows the selected northwestern bend west into Tweedsmuir; the fishing map continues the Dean route while distinguishing the northern Itasyuko River branch from Sigutlat Lake. The selection remains on the westward/southwestern Dean course and does not traverse that lateral lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Supported at ordinary generalized corridor scale.
correspondence.name_limit: Sigutlat Lake and Itasyuko River are distinct side-system labels, not names for the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Takia junction and westward Dean toward the lower fragment
correspondence.finding: The original fishing map identifies the major Takia River entering from the east/southeast at the lower end of the Dean’s southern turn; the selected Dean turns west. Crag Creek and subsequent lower tributary settings orient the continuation into the fragment spanning the lower river. Neither Takia nor lateral creeks are included as selected headwater branches.
correspondence.correspondence: Major junction and fragment transition supported at generalized scale; no pointwise boundary claim.
correspondence.name_limit: Dean is the trunk label; Takia and Crag are lateral names.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Dean bends, canyon and actual Dean Channel terminal
correspondence.finding: The Guardian original Figure1 and provincial fishing map both show the lower corridor, including the prominent northern bend, return west past the lower tributary network, lower canyon and final southward mouth reach into Dean Channel near Kimsquit. The observed mouth corresponds to the actual selected terminal; it is not inferred merely from coastal basin membership.
